subject: Benchmark methodology exchange \u0014 prompt sets, eval harness, measurement defs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgefin.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, Mar 1, 2026 at 15:12 PST
Subject: Recap + next steps  performance targets and benchmark methodology

Hi Samir  thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned before we design the benchmark:

- Targets you mentioned: 95th percentile latency <= 120ms for short completions (~32 tokens), sustained throughput of ~250 req/s at 16 concurrent streams, and streaming support for partial token delivery to the client.
- Important constraints: end-to-end latency measured from our edge ingress to final token emitted, prefer TLS termination at customer edge; KV cache warm-up should be documented.
- You asked for a reproducible benchmark and for us to share prompt sets / eval harness so EdgeFin can validate locally.

Attached: initial prompt set (benchmark_prompt_set_v2.jsonl) and a short eval_harness_readme. Proposal: we run a Redwood-hosted benchmark run first (to validate our runner and configs) and then hand over the harness for EdgeFin to reproduce on your infra.

Please confirm the latency/throughput numbers above and whether the concurrency model should be steady-state 16 concurrent connections or a bursty mix (e.g., 4s ramp to 16). If we get confirmation, we will share the detailed measurement definitions and an annotated command-line to run the harness.

Thanks 
Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark_prompt_set_v2.jsonl, eval_harness_readme.md

On Mon, Mar 1, 2026 at 3:12 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Samir  thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned before we design the benchmark:
> 
> - Targets you mentioned: 95th percentile latency <= 120ms for short completions (~32 tokens), sustained throughput of ~250 req/s at 16 concurrent streams, and streaming support for partial token delivery to the client.
> 
> Attached: initial prompt set (benchmark_prompt_set_v2.jsonl) and a short eval_harness_readme. Proposal: we run a Redwood-hosted benchmark run first (to validate our runner and configs) and then hand over the harness for EdgeFin to reproduce on your infra.

Thanks for the clear summary, Marissa  that matches our expectations. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: 95th <= 120ms is accurate for the short path (32 tokens). For longer tails (>=128 tokens) we care about median latency per 32-token window.
- Throughput/concurrency: steady-state 16 concurrent streaming connections is preferred. We also want a 10-minute soak test at target throughput to ensure no memory growth.
- Streaming: we need partial token delivery within 25ms after generation on the server side (client buffering tolerated up to 10ms).
- Reproducibility: yes  we will need the exact seed, model config (quantization, KV cache behavior), and the harness version. We'll attach our internal test spec (see eng@edgefin.com message attached).

If you can provide the annotated measurement definitions (p95 calculation method, warm-up exclusion rules, error handling), we can review and confirm. We would like Redwood to run the hosted benchmark the week of Mar 8 and share raw traces (CSV/JSON) and the harness commands so we can run the same tests on our staging cluster.

Samir
S. Patel
Head of Platform, EdgeFin

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, Mar 4, 2026 at 09:18 PST
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + next steps  benchmark clarifications (internal)

Marissa / Steph  quick draft of the measurement definitions and run plan below. I'll push the runner and the Docker tag to our internal registry tonight and share the exact command tomorrow.

Run plan (short):
- Model: redwood-open-3B-quant (config: 8-bit quant, per-channel; KV cache enabled)
- Prompt set: benchmark_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (50k lines; short/mid/long buckets labeled)
- Warm-up: first 60s ignored for metrics; separate warm-up traffic with same concurrency.
- Concurrency: steady 16 connections using HTTP/2 streaming; 250 req/s sustained for 10m soak; ramp: linear 30s to target.
- Latency measurement: measure server-sent event timestamp delta (server generation->network emit) plus ingress e2e delta. p95 calculated across per-request total latency excluding warm-up. For long responses we compute sliding-window p50/p95 per 32-token window.
- Error handling: any 5xx or stream aborted counts as a failed request; we'll report failure rate and exclude failed requests from latency quartiles but report both inclusive and exclusive stats.
- Reproducibility: runner will accept --seed, --model-config-hash, and a manifest.json listing prompt checksums. We'll include Docker image tag: redwood/bench-runner:20260304-candidate.

Deliverables to EdgeFin after hosted run:
- Raw traces (JSONL) + CSV summary, p95/p50 for each bucket, failure rate, CPU/GPU utilization charts, and the runner command + Docker tag. We'll redact any internal server IPs per Steph's guidance.

Mateo
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
